# Quality-Control & Quality-Assurance for Metabolomics

Omics data can be messy. Anywhere from tens to thousands of features (genes, transcripts, exons, metabolites, or proteins) are measured in a high-throughput manner across several samples from multiple phenotypes. Although metabolomics doesn't have a single measure for the quality of a metabolite abundance, nor the ability to judge the quality of the equivalent of called bases, there are many measures of experiment quality that can be measured and reported. \n\n Our quality-control and quality-assurance (QC/QA) pipeline (see @fig-pipeline) was designed to assign quality metrics to all of the Metabolomics Workbench datasets (analyses) we could download in July of 2026.


![Overview of the QC/QA pipeline, starting from repaired and harmonized data ingestion, to generation of HTML reports.](posterimages/qcqa_pipeline_pipeline_lucid_2026-11-05.png){#fig-pipeline}


# Metabolomics Workbench

- NIH Common Fund's National Metabolomics Data Repository.
- Established in 2012.
- Organized by:
  - Project: a biological question, contains one or more **related** studies.
  - Study: contains one or more analyses.
  - Analysis: typically one analysis method or sample type, e.g. NMR, MS + chromatography, +ve / -ve mode, etc.
- Currently hosts 4261 studies, from 60 countries.
  - 7240 analysis datasets (2026-07-21).
- Our lab has years of experience working with MW data [@thompsonMajorUpdateImproved2026a; @powellMwtabPythonLibrary2021; @smelterPythonLibraryFAIRer2018; @thompsonMESSESSoftwareTransforming2023a; @powellMetabolomicsWorkbenchFile2023].

# Number of Samples in SSF Groups

```{=typst}
#columns(2, gutter: 2pt)[
```

- Subject sample factors (SSFs):
  - One or more experimentally important metadata about the samples.
  - E.g. Cancerous vs normal, high-fat diet vs normal diet, etc.
- We combine multiple SSFs to make a unique label that defines the **experimental groups** of samples.
- Additional sample data includes things like the raw file name, biological replicate.
- The number of samples per SSF group indicates if the experimental design is statistically powerful or not, based on general rule of thumb.
- The counts are **after** removing samples with < 10 present metabolites and any outliers.

```{=typst}
#colbreak()
```

# Percent Missingness & Left-Censorship

High percentage of missing values, especially without the indication of left-censorship (LC); indicates the presence of possible data quality issues.

![Number of datasets by their percent missing, colored by status.](`r gsub("docs/", "", colored_cutoffs_files$pm$file)`){#fig-pm}



# Maximum Observed Median Relative Standard Deviation (RSD)

High maximum observed median RSD indicates high variability in the measurements.

![Number of datasets by the maximum observed median RSD, colored by status.](`r gsub("docs/", "", colored_cutoffs_files$rsd$file)`){#fig-rsd}



# Median Within SSF Group Sample-Sample Correlations

Low maximum median within SSF group sample-sample ICI-Kt correlations [@flightInformationContentInformedKendallTauCorrelation2026] indicate high biological variance between samples.

![Number of datasets by their maximum median within SSF group sample-sample ICI-Kt, colored by status.](`r gsub("docs/", "", colored_cutoffs_files$med_cor$file)`){#fig-med-cor}



# Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Scores - PC-90

As more principal components (PC) are needed to account for 90% of the variance in the data (PC-90), it indicates weak signal variance within the dataset in comparison to other sources of variance present.

![Number of datasets by the Log10 of the principal component that contains 90% of the variance in the data (PC-90), colored by status.](`r gsub("docs/", "", colored_cutoffs_files$pc_90$file)`){#fig-pc-90}


```{=typst}
#colbreak()
```

# PCA Scores - ANOVA

Lack of separation of SSF groups across meaningful PCs indicates weak signal variance within the dataset.

$$\text{status}_{anova} = \begin{cases} 
  \text{green} & \text{if}\  \ \text{SSF} \ \text{p}_{adj} \le 0.05 \ \& \ \text{PC}\text{perc} \gt 5 \% \\
  \text{yellow} & \text{if}\  \ \text{SSF} \ \text{p}_{adj} \le 0.05 \ \& \ \text{PC}\text{perc} \gt 1 \% \ \text{or} \ \text{Add} \ \text{p}_{adj} \le 0.05 \ \& \ \text{PC}\text{perc} \gt 5 \%\\
  \text{red} & \text{if}\  \ \text{SSF} \ \text{p}_{adj} \le 0.05 \ \& \ \text{PC}\text{perc} \lt 1 \% \ \text{or} \ \text{SSF} \ \text{p}_{adj} \gt 0.05\\
   \end{cases}
$$

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-green-1
#| fig-cap: Examples of low and high p-value ANOVA PC scores.
pca_example_green_1 + pca_example_red_1
```

# Detecting the Presence of Likely Confounding Factors

* Possible confounding factors can be detected using Hartigan's dip test for multi-modal distributions [@hartiganDipTestUnimodality1985] on the sample scores by SSF group on PC1 and PC2.
* When there is additional sample factors present, they can be checked to see if adding it to the SSFs removes the multi-modal distribution, or improves the ANOVA results compared to the original SSFs.
* We detected **XXX (X%)** datasets with likely confounding factors, and of those, **XXX (X%)** appear to have an additional sample factor that when included removes the confounding.

```{r}
#| label: confounding-example-plot-6863
#| fig-cap: "PCA plots for dataset AN006863. **A**: Histogram of sample scores for the two SSF groups on PC1. **B**: Histogram of sample scores for the two SSF groups on PC2. **C**: Sample scores on PC1 and PC2, colored by SSF group. **D**: Sina and boxplots of sample scores on PC1 by an additional sample subject data, cohort."
#| fig-height: 8
example_confound_plot_6863$pc1_histogram + example_confound_plot_6863$pc2_histogram + example_confound_plot_6863$scores + free(example_confound_plot_6863$confound_sinaplot) + plot_layout(ncol = 2, nrow = 2) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

# Detection of Technical Replicates

Technical replicates can be detected through a combination of:

* unusually high sample-sample correlation;
* unusually low differences in sample IDs;
* runs of both when arranged by hiearchical clustering.

```{r}
#| label: fig-technical-replicates
#| fig-cap: "**A**: Sample-sample correlation heatmap showing technical replicates; **B**: point plot of correlation distances and string distances between samples, with replicates noted in red; **C**: Sina plot of total RSD, technical RSD, and non-technical RSD for datasets with technical replicates."
#| fig-height: 8
heatmap_grob = grid::grid.grabExpr(ComplexHeatmap::draw(technical_replicates_plot$heatmap))

layout = "ABBB
CCCC"
free(wrap_elements(heatmap_grob)) + technical_replicates_plot$dotplot + non_technical_rsd_plot + plot_layout(design = layout) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```
